messages.text: Norris claims Sao Paulo GP pole after treacherous rain-hit qualifying

metadata.summary: Lando Norris claimed pole position after a hugely-challenging Sao Paulo Grand Prix qualifying in treacherous wet conditions, for a race that will see Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen start at the back of the grid.
metadata.content: Sao Paulo GP Qualifying: Lando Norris claims rain-hit pole in wild conditions with Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen to start at back | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Breaking Sao Paulo GP Qualifying: Lando Norris claims rain-hit pole in wild conditions with Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen to start at back Lando Norris tames awful wet conditions for his third Brazil pole in a row; Frustrated Russell drops down from second with grid penalty; Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen starting 20th and 21st; watch Sunday's Sao Paulo GP live at 5pm on Sky Sports F1, build-up from 3.30pm Saturday 7 November 2026 21:50, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Grand Prix. Lando Norris claimed pole position after a hugely-challenging Sao Paulo Grand Prix qualifying in treacherous wet conditions, for a race that will see Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen start at the back of the grid. On a typically rain-hit day at ever-unpredictable Interlagos, qualifying was suspended for over an hour and 20 minutes after a torrential downpour hit the drivers' first laps of Q1. The rain eventually eased - but never particularly stopped - to allow running take place and create a thrilling and unpredictable battle for pole. metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton reveals details of talks with Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc in Brazil after Mexico fall out | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lewis Hamilton reveals details of talks with Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc in Brazil after Mexico fall out Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc held talks with Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur in Brazil following their contentious opening lap incident last time out in Mexico; watch Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix live at 5pm on Sky Sports F1, build-up from 3.30pm Saturday 7 November 2026 22:14, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Sao Paulo Grand Prix Lewis Hamilton says he and Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc have "squashed" their incident at the Mexico City Grand Prix after holding talks in Brazil. Hamilton, Leclerc and team principal Frederic Vasseur held talks on Thursday night to discuss the incident which saw Max Verstappen take advantage of the opening lap Ferrari squabble last Sunday to win the race. Hamilton has subsequently been critical of Leclerc in interviews and said that discussions were required to more clearly define their rules of combat to avoid costly repeats in future. messages.text: 'A different Noni?' Madueke finding a new level for Arsenal

metadata.summary: Noni Madueke lay sprawled on the turf, head in his hands, following his one-on-one miss late in Arsenal's 1-0 victory over Hull. His frustration continued to show even after the final whistle.
metadata.content: Noni Madueke has become a 'different' player, says Mikel Arteta, as winger finds new level of creativity and efficiency | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Noni Madueke has become a 'different' player, says Mikel Arteta, as winger finds new level of creativity and efficiency Noni Madueke starred in Arsenal's 1-0 win over Hull as the Gunners moved six points clear at the top of the Premier League; former Chelsea winger is creating more chances than anyone else in the division and has become a "different" player, says Mikel Arteta Nick Wright Football Features Writer @nicholaspwright Saturday 7 November 2026 22:08, UK Image: Noni Madueke helped Arsenal claim a 1-0 win over Hull Noni Madueke lay sprawled on the turf, head in his hands, following his one-on-one miss late in Arsenal's 1-0 victory over Hull . His frustration continued to show even after the final whistle. The winger's reaction showed the standards this "different Noni", to quote Mikel Arteta, is setting himself as he strives to reach another level. Bukayo Saka's injury was a significant setback to Arsenal. Madueke has made it his mission to soften the blow. So far, he has filled in impressively. Arteta understood his demeanour after the game. "He knew he had three clear chances to score," he said, always demanding more. But there was also an acknowledgement of his crucial role in Martin Odegaard's goal.
